scope: Research only; not approved for installation, no READY, species or schedule edits.
evidence_method: Reused completed taxonomy; morphology paraphrased from cited sources. Photo captions are leads, not image identity clearance. Arnoglossum full-text retrieval limitation is explicit.

species.look_here_first: Inspect a leaf from both sides and trace its veins from the base. Then examine the tiny clustered flowers and mature capsules, rather than identifying the shrub from flower color alone.
morphology_keys: Bushy low shrub.
Leaves narrow toward the attachment and have rounded marginal teeth.
Lower leaf surface bears soft hairs.
Small five-petaled flowers produce capsules that open at maturity.
photo_roles: Whole flowering branch and leaf attachment.
Upper and lower leaf surfaces with vein origins visible.
Flower cluster and mature capsule with millimeter scale.
species.lookalike_work: Compare with Ceanothus americanus using a regional leaf and inflorescence key; source-backed exact separating measurements remain pending.

photo_leads.creator_as_captioned: David Parke, Southwestern School of Botanical Medicine

species.look_here_first: Examine a broad, flattened spikelet hanging from a drooping branch. Confirm that it contains multiple florets and photograph the leaf blade, sheath and collar on the same plant.
morphology_keys: Upright, clump-forming perennial grass.
Open panicle with nodding branches.
Broad, flattened spikelets contain multiple florets.
Leaf blades are relatively broad and flat.
photo_roles: Spikelet face and edge with millimeter scale.
Floret and glume details; blade-sheath junction and ligule.
species.lookalike_work: The common name wild oats is shared with unrelated grasses. Distinguish from Avena and other Chasmanthium with spikelet architecture and a regional key.

species.look_here_first: Spread a submerged shoot in a shallow tray of water. Photograph an entire leaf whorl and the narrow, forked leaf segments, then magnify the small teeth and any fruits.
morphology_keys: Submerged, rootless perennial aquatic herb.
Divided leaves occur in whorls.
Leaf segments have small teeth.
Tiny flowers occur near leaf bases.
photo_roles: Submerged shoot in water with whorls separated.
One whole leaf on a scale and magnified teeth.
Mature fruit from the same verified plant, if available.
species.lookalike_work: UF/IFAS flags Cabomba caroliniana as a confuser. Exact separation from other Ceratophyllum needs a regional leaf/fruit key; do not assume aquarium labels establish species.

species.look_here_first: Check the thick, nearly round leaf and its attachment to the twig. Pair this with a flower raceme or an attached fruit cluster; large round leaves alone are not enough.
morphology_keys: Woody shrub or tree with alternate simple leaves.
Leaves are leathery, nearly circular and usually have conspicuous reddish veins.
Small flowers are arranged along racemes.
Female plants bear clusters of fleshy fruits.
photo_roles: Mature leaf upper and lower surfaces with twig attachment.
Flower raceme or attached fruit cluster.
species.lookalike_work: Compare with other cultivated Coccoloba using adult leaves and reproductive structures; do not infer Texas native status from a Florida source.

species.look_here_first: Look for solitary flowers at the forks of low, wiry shoots. Photograph the funnel-shaped corolla from the side and the five-lobed calyx that surrounds the mature capsule.
morphology_keys: Small perennial with several basal stems and short hairs.
Simple leaves are alternate with entire margins.
Flowers are solitary at branch forks, with a five-lobed funnel-shaped corolla.
Persistent calyx largely encloses a four-valved capsule.
photo_roles: Complete shoot showing branching and leaf arrangement.
Flower front and profile with scale.
Fruiting calyx and an already opened capsule.
species.lookalike_work: Compare small petunia-like Solanaceae using calyx, corolla and fruit. Local species-level comparison remains pending; preserve source aliases from the taxonomy records.

species.look_here_first: Inspect the grooved stem and the cylindrical heads in the broad flowering cluster. A close-up should resolve the five equal, keeled bracts around one head.
morphology_keys: Stem has low angles and descending ridges associated with leaves.
Numerous heads form a broad, relatively flat-topped array.
Each head has one series of five equal, keeled phyllaries.
photo_roles: Whole plant including basal and upper leaves.
Single head profile and underside resolving phyllary count and keels.
species.lookalike_work: Name does not mean Plantago. Exact comparison with other Arnoglossum and full leaf description remain pending.
